brief: A small-parts organizer with at least six separate bins.

requirements.evidence: Six-cell hex cluster with shallow half-depth bins sized for small parts. Sample screws, nuts, standoffs, tape, solder and tweezers are placed in them.
Six separate bins (hex-bin-half), one each in cells (0,0), (1,0), (2,0), (-1,1), (0,1) and (1,1).

finish.summary: I built a small-parts organiser from six hex cells in two rows of three. Each cell has its own half-depth drop-in bin, so there are six separate bins. I capped all the open outer faces and bolted the joints between cells so the cells stay together. To show what it's for, I put sample parts in the bins: M3 screws, nuts and standoffs, a roll of electrical tape, a solder reel and tweezers. These sit below the bin rims and can be seen from above. The final check found no rule errors, and the parts were checked for collisions and nothing overlaps. The build has 30 parts, and the print estimate is about 2.65 kg of filament.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
